policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'And I said unto them', a first-person singular consecutive imperfect matching the qere וָאֹמַר; the ketiv ויאמר would give third-person 'And he said', which the ASV does not render.

ASV text reads 'Nephushesim', transliterating the ketiv נפושסים with u in the second syllable; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Nephishesim' relegates the qere נְפִישְׁסִים to the margin.
